And if I could -- the attack, according to this document, on page 2, third paragraph down, was to commence at 5.00 in the morning on the 26th. And if we go to paragraph 8 on that same page, it says, "Carry out artillery preparations for attack by firing at significant targets in Demisevci village, Bonjancic and the Mahala and Otoka neighbourhoods." Do you know from the documentation that you observed what happened in Mahala and Otoka?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware not from the documentation, but I am aware that -- that this attack did occur.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And at the end of this document, then, Mr. Brown, on page 3, paragraph 15, it says, at the last subpart of that, it says, "Upon completion of the task, take the prisoners to the sports hall of the secondary school centre and hand over the war booty to the Sanski Most Serbian TO staff." Earlier you discussed a pattern. Does this document reflect that pattern that you've been testifying about, Mr. Brown? Can you comment on that?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think it does. It brings together some of the threads: Cooperation between the TO, 6th Brigade; it brings together that there was to be artillery preparation. That generally means firing on targets. It's targeted against a non-Serb area. Complete control is to be achieved of the area. And I know from the Sanski Most police document and also from the CSB-compiled report that the sports hall was used as a detention centre where people were brought to. So it corroborates that document also, and - - and I think it's -- it's a -- it's a document with many components. It would seem to highlight that -- that issue of -- of a pattern.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could turn to tab 82. I'd like your interpretation of this document, please, Mr. Brown. This is a 1 Krajina Corps report dated the 31st of May, 1992, that goes to the Main Staff of the Bosnian Serb army, and it is signed by General Talic. I'd like to direct your attention to the second page, ERN number 00867035, and under 5, subpart B, it reads, "After the actions in Kozarac, Kljuc, and Sanski Most, some conscripts of Muslim nationality have asked to be released from the units. They expressed their dissatisfaction with the massive destruction of their towns." It goes on to say in that paragraph, "This is made worse by public statements made in the media by SDS Bosanska Krajina Autonomous Region leaders who advocate moving and expelling all Muslims and Croats from these areas." Mr. Brown, how do you interpret this paragraph? In particular, in light of the earlier document that we saw that referenced attacks in Sanski Most. Is there any connection?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think there is. It comes only a few days after the attack. An order was issued. It highlights there has been significant destruction in those municipalities and that there's an advocation that people should be moved out and -- and expelled from Muslim and Croat -- or Muslims and Croats should be expelled from those areas. And there are other references in this document. For example, on page 1, at the very bottom of the page, "In the municipality of Kljuc, suburban areas are being cleared and the weapons seized in Muslim-populated villages," highlighting here that the target is Muslim villages. I think it's -- it's a -- a document indicating where the actions are occurring at that time, that the military are involved in those actions, and that there's significant destruction as a result of those actions, and that this issue of expelling and moving people out is known.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to talk, Mr. Brown, on the topic of -- what the documentation showed on the killing of civilians, the 1 KK documentation showed. And if we could start first with the document that's found at tab 82.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just ask one question in between --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in relation to -- You read about the -- the dissatisfaction with the massive destruction of their towns expressed by conscripts of Muslim nationality. What could you tell us about the presence still on the 31st of May, 1992, of conscripts of Muslim nationality? We heard quite some evidence on officers that for whatever reason left their units or -- how about the conscripts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the percentage or numbers in the 1st Krajina Corps. It was not an area that I was able to -- to look at, and I didn't get information outside this particular report. As you say, I was made aware of the documentation relating to officers, and they -- them being placed on leave and sent -- sent away in June. But I don't -- I don't know of the figures of Muslim conscripts that were serving in the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's -- can we turn to the document that is found at tab 82.1. And I'd like to address -- ask you, Mr. Brown: First of all, in the documentation that you reviewed, did you see references to the killing of civilians or people in the custody of the Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were a number of references directly to killings of civilians and others in the 1st Krajina Corps report, and I think I addressed that in the report. In a number -- there were a number -- a number of examples.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you -- generally -- generally - and we'll get to the documentation in a minute - tell the Court what was the reaction of the military authorities to these killings of civilians? What did you see in the documentation?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that -- that question's incredibly general for such an important area. If the witness can refer the Trial Chamber to specific documents in that regard, that, of course, I think, will be more helpful than a generalised question and a generalised answer of that nature, I would submit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least it's not leading, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you answer the question and be as specific as possible on your sources.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only remember of one documented incident of killing that I saw an element of follow-up through the military judicial process, and that related to a document or a series of documents relating to a killing in Kljuc in 1992 at the school, Velagici School. However, when I followed or we followed the documentary trail through -- through the military court records, there appeared to be a tailoring off, although there was initially some people rounded up and held, there was a tailoring of the investigation -- a tailing-off of the investigation, and nothing appeared to happen as a result of that. I do not remember seeing any other examples whereby the killings that were referenced in the 1 Krajina Corps documents resulted in any apparent follow-up from the documents that I was able to see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you specifically talking now about killings of civilians, or are you talking about people being killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, predominantly killings of civilians, or massacres, they would sometimes call them. I'm not talking about killings like, say, combat deaths.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, I'm looking at the clock. It's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I can just -- if I can just have one additional document that Mr. Brown referenced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's found in tab 82.1, and this is the regular combat report of the 4th of November, 1992, again 1st Krajina Corps. It goes to the Main Staff of the army, and it is a document that was prepared by and signed by Colonel Vukelic. And, Mr. Brown, if you'd take a look at paragraph 2, the second paragraph in paragraph 2. Could you comment on this -- this paragraph that references a massacre -- a brutal massacre.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Actually just to finish the question that the -- Judge Orie placed to me, it was civilians or prisoners. And this was one -- either killings of civilians or prisoners. This is one example whereby they reference the killings of prisoners. And in Kotor Varos, although there had been military operations in there in June, there was a small pocket that held out through most of the summer and into the autumn of 1992 in Vecici. That group -- there were references in the Krajina reports that they were negotiating how to resolve that and whether that group was going to be moved out. And whilst that negotiation was underway, men appeared to have broken out of this small pocket in Kotor Varos, but they were captured. And this document on the 4th of November references that they were -- they were -- they were captured and a brutal massacre occurred on that group in Vecici. The subsequent documents on the 1st Krajina Corps - and I do reference this issue in the report - the subsequent documents are -- characterise that group as combat deaths. And I'm aware that the Kotor Varos Light Infantry Brigade commander continued in his command at least until 1993, from documentation I've reviewed. So I think here was an example of a large-scale killing of people who'd been captured in Kotor Varos; it was initially reported as a brutal massacre. I believe in the following-on days it was portrayed as combat casualties, and I'm aware that nothing -- or from the documentation anyway, I'm aware that nothing -- nothing came of this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's three minutes past 7.00. We'll adjourn until tomorrow, quarter past 2.00, same courtroom. I inform the parties that arrangements have been made to continue on Thursday morning. We'll adjourn until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 13th day of July, 2005, at 2.15 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25
